every bear pitch I've seen on NVDA looks something like this

never "they're gonna miss EPS" or "gross margins will be 80% instead of 85%"

always "on page 46 of the 2023 10-Q you can see that Restricted Cash is overstated by $4.56B and that their Corporate Debt Securities balance is amortizing at a rate which indicates cookie-jar accounting, plus spring-loading of all purchase-price allocation to an offshore JV, which we calculate as a headwind of $7M, and when paired with bloated working capital metrics, such as inventories rising year-over-year by 45 bps, our due diligence has revealed that $3 trillion dollars of NVDA chips are in a Taiwanese dumpster. Google Maps confirms our 'dumpster-stuffing' thesis, and the balance increases to $3.1 trillion when using MACRS depreciation (preferred for GIPS compliance, per CFA level 2)."

"We believe that the other $2 trillion of chips are somewhere in Boston, with local TMT funds burying excess inventory everywhere from Saugus to Springfield (an area known as "The S-Curve"). Next quarter, NVDA will be forced to write-down this $5T of inventory to $0, which, given NVDA's current market cap of $5T, and based on our own S-curve analysis, would yield a new market cap of $0. Our full S-curve deck is available on Substack for paid subs only, where we recommend continuing to buy the $5 strike NVDA puts, same ones as Burry, expiring next Friday."

(Note: while we recommend subs buy these puts, we have been selling them to you, as has Burry, which is how the S-Curve works in technology investing -- we have sold so many NVDA puts to subs that we are 99% of the 2026 open interest. Think AAPL, Blackberry, shit like that. In next week's Substack, we will do a deep dive on Saugus, MA, where channel checks show that NVDA has been dumping graphics cards on Route 1 near the old Kowloon.)
